<!-- verdify-paused-handoff-20261012:965 -->
Jason's shutdown handoff: **implementation and delivery PAUSED; do not auto-resume.**

**Current state:** API fix is native-qualified in PR970 and combined PR973: authenticated HTTP501 without opening DB or fabricating observed equipment history. No exact-image production adoption/live contract receipt exists. Retained history audit cannot classify older/rotated intent rows; do not rewrite history or infer resource credit.

**Blockers:** Jason explicitly paused all implementation/delivery. The listed acceptance boundary remains unproved beyond linked historical receipts.

**Next step on explicit resume:** After explicit Jason resume, refresh exact source/live and predecessor evidence, then satisfy: Either return an explicit unsupported/disabled result without writing observed history, or deliver a typed command through the existing owning HA/setpoint writer with authorization, idempotency and terminal failure semantics. Do not introduce a second device writer.

**Acceptance retained:**
- [ ] Either return an explicit unsupported/disabled result without writing observed history, or deliver a typed command through the existing owning HA/setpoint writer with authorization, idempotency and terminal failure semantics. Do not introduce a second device writer.
- [ ] Only authentic source-bound readback writes observed equipment state. A requested on command while real state remains off cannot fabricate an on interval or resource credit.
- [ ] Focused positive and rejected/failed/timeout tests distinguish intent, delivery and observation; ordinary auth and greenhouse/circuit boundaries hold.
- [ ] Exact source/digest/config adoption and read-only live contract verification are published. Any physical command test has a bounded operator-safe scope and actual observation; no live command is sent merely for triage.
- [ ] Existing affected history is audited for provenance and explicitly bounded; no broad rewrite of historical outcomes, assigned-day denominators or resource claims.
